quote: Could you just read me off your home address, and I can look up the next one?
stewart_read: Nearly two minutes were spent on address confusion before the rep asked the customer to just read it off — should have been the first move, not the last resort.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive: rep tried to guess the address from system data before falling back to asking directly, wasting time rather than executing a deliberate strategy.
coaching_implication: Default to asking the customer to state their address rather than guessing off system data with a garbled record.

quote: Not entirely too much because at the moment, it's just me... I would say it's probably about $300 or so, not not too much.
stewart_read: The bill was captured cleanly at $300/month but the rep's response was purely transactional acknowledgment, not a flip into savings/pain framing.
coaching_implication: Reflect the $300 back as the number solar replaces — e.g. tie it forward to the guaranteed-savings pitch line rather than just moving to the next verify item.

quote: About 300 a month? K. Yeah. Yeah. No problem. We can still cut that down for you a little bit.
stewart_read: This is the closest the rep gets to a flip — acknowledging the bill can be cut down — but it's a soft, hedged line ('cut that down a little bit') rather than a firm reframe against the utility.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: the softness could be intentional pacing to avoid over-selling before qualifying credit, but the line is too weak to count as a full flip.
coaching_implication: Strengthen the flip language — tie the $300 explicitly to the guaranteed savings program right after capturing it.

quote: I own couple real estate, you know, rent renting and all that. I own a couple Airbnbs.
stewart_read: Customer owning multiple rental properties/Airbnbs is a strong qualification signal (property owner, investment mindset, possible multi-property solar or roofing interest) that the rep never revisits.
coaching_implication: Should have asked whether the Airbnb/rental properties also have high energy usage or are candidates for solar/roofing — a cross-sell and qualification opportunity left unexplored.

quote: I can just send you a text from my personal phone
stewart_read: Rep offers a personal phone number for bill follow-up, the flagged anti-pattern for privacy/scale exposure noted in the schema's bill capture roadmap section.
coaching_implication: Should route bill follow-up through the company line/automated process, not personal number, per the schema's detection_today anti_pattern note.

quote: I'll just I'll send you the I'll send you, like, a text just from my regular number
stewart_read: The call ends without any appointment_set attempt, no time anchor, no 'is that fair' handshake — just a bill-text promise and goodbye.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: rep may be deferring appointment-setting until bill is received, but nothing in the transcript states this is the plan or commits to a follow-up call time.
coaching_implication: Even without the bill in hand, the rep should have proposed a tentative appointment window or committed to a specific callback time before ending the call.
